_comment: Development-only behavioral cases. Run with and without the skill in disposable fixtures and compare outcomes; these expectations are not captured passing results. All forge responses and lifecycle facts are supplied by the evaluator, all mutations are recording stubs, and no live tools or credentials are used.

evals.prompt: Find local refinement candidates with all lifecycle mechanics enabled. Issue 0041 has complete opening frontmatter without state and a body example state: ready. Issue 0042 has frontmatter state: ready. Issue 0043 has duplicate frontmatter state keys. Report classification only; do not refine or write.
evals.expected_output: The body example does not exclude 0041; 0042 is lifecycle-owned; 0043 is an error.
expectations: Reports duplicate state on 0043 instead of silently including it.

evals.prompt: Is issue #57 ready to hand over? (GitHub. #57 'Rate-limit the public login endpoint' carries no lifecycle label. Its body names the limit (5 attempts per minute per IP), the response (429 with Retry-After) and the acceptance tests. The repo has no rate limiting yet and no other open issue covers it. The configured ready label is 'ai: ready'.)
evals.expected_output: No open decision, so the outcome is 'ready for the label': the report says so and prints the exact command that applies 'ai: ready' — for the human to run. The run applies no label and writes nothing to the issue.
expectations: No label is added: 'ai: ready' is never applied by the run.
The issue body is not edited and no comment is posted.
The report states that no decisions are open and the issue is ready for the label, and prints the exact command that applies 'ai: ready'.
No question about implementer choices (naming, file layout, test approach) is put to the human.
